heading: INT. MUNICIPAL WATERWORKS PUMP HOUSE - NIGHT

units.text: INT. MUNICIPAL WATERWORKS PUMP HOUSE - NIGHT
A cathedral of riveted iron and brass, three stories high, lit by one amber work lamp.
Steam pipes sweat along the walls.
The great pump wheel turns overhead with a patient, heavy rhythm, and behind a brick archway, a vault door the color of old pennies.
SILAS "THE ACCOUNTANT" BRANNIGAN, fifties, silver hair, wire spectacles, wears a gray overcoat and a face like a closed ledger.
He kneels at the vault, ear to the steel.
LORETTA "LOLLY" DUCHAMP, forties, a redhead in a mechanic's coverall, holds a stopwatch and a flashlight.
MARCUS JEROME FALK, thirties, tall and broad, wears a night watchman's cap two sizes too small, and sweats through it.
NELL PETRAKIS, twenties, sits on a crate with a tool roll across her knees, pale and unblinking.
Four minutes before the watchman's round.
units.name: SILAS

units.text: Three and a half. He's early on Thursdays.
units.name: LOLLY

units.text: He's early because the Missus makes him.
units.name: MARCUS

units.text: Nell unrolls the tools, hands him a slim steel bit.
The pump wheel overhead thumps like a heart.
